questions.question: What is a renewable resource?
choices: A resource replenished naturally on a relevant human time scale
A resource that can never be depleted
Any resource formed deep underground
A resource used only once

questions.question: Which resource is nonrenewable on human time scales?
choices: Sunlight
Wind
Coal
Flowing water

questions.question: What does resource conservation mean?
choices: Using a resource as quickly as possible
Ending all use of every natural material
Replacing all renewable resources with fossil fuels
Reducing unnecessary use and protecting supplies

questions.question: What is reuse?
choices: Breaking a material into raw inputs
Using an item again without first processing it into raw material
Discarding a product after one use
Burning a material to obtain energy

questions.question: What is recycling?
choices: Storing every discarded item indefinitely
Using a product again without processing
Using only newly mined resources
Processing discarded materials into materials for new products

questions.question: What is a watershed?
choices: An area of land that drains to a common water body
A layer of rock with no water movement
An isolated cloud above a forest
Only the deepest part of an ocean

questions.question: What does biodiversity refer to?
choices: Only the number of people in a region
Only the age of a forest
The variety of life, including genetic, species, and ecosystem diversity
The amount of rainfall in one storm

questions.question: Why can a renewable forest resource still be depleted?
choices: Trees cannot regrow under any conditions
Harvesting can exceed regrowth and damage the ecosystem
All forests grow at the same rate
Renewable means that harvesting has no effect

questions.question: Why can reducing consumption save more resources than recycling alone?
choices: Recycling always uses more resources than making new products
It avoids some material extraction and production before waste is created
Consumption has no connection to waste
All materials can be recycled indefinitely without losses

questions.question: How can excess fertilizer runoff harm a lake?
choices: It can promote algal growth whose decomposition reduces dissolved oxygen
It directly turns fresh water into salt water
It prevents all plant growth immediately
It always cools the water below freezing

questions.question: Why can vegetation along a stream help protect water quality?
choices: It prevents all rainfall from reaching the stream
It produces unlimited clean water
It makes pollutants evaporate instantly
It can trap sediment and reduce nutrient runoff

questions.question: Why should environmental decisions consider a product's entire life cycle?
choices: Only disposal has environmental effects
Only manufacturing uses energy
Extraction, production, use, and disposal can each have impacts
Transport cannot affect resource use

questions.question: What distinguishes energy efficiency from simply using a device less often?
choices: Efficiency means replacing all electricity with chemical fuel
Efficiency means using the same device for fewer hours only
Efficiency measures total fuel use without considering output
Efficiency provides a comparable service using less energy

questions.question: Why can groundwater be depleted despite being replenished by rain?
choices: Groundwater cannot move through rock
Withdrawal can exceed the rate of recharge
Rainwater never reaches underground aquifers
Every aquifer refills completely each day

questions.question: Why can habitat fragmentation reduce biodiversity?
choices: It can isolate populations and limit movement between habitats
It guarantees that all species adapt quickly
It always increases habitat size
It removes all competition among organisms

questions.question: A forest regrows 100 units of timber yearly but loses 150 units to harvest yearly. What does this pattern suggest if it continues?
choices: The timber supply must increase
Harvest and regrowth are balanced
The timber supply will decline
Regrowth will automatically increase to match harvest

questions.question: Two lamps provide the same useful light, but one uses half as much electricity. Which lamp is more energy-efficient?
choices: Both must have the same efficiency
The lamp using twice as much electricity
The lamp using half as much electricity
Efficiency cannot be compared without knowing their color

questions.question: A town wants to reduce discarded drink containers. Which action most directly prevents waste generation?
choices: Increase production of disposable containers
Send every container to a larger landfill
Collect more containers only after disposal
Use durable refillable containers repeatedly

questions.question: A proposed energy project has low operating emissions but affects wildlife habitat. What is a sound evaluation approach?
choices: Ignore habitat effects because emissions are low
Compare multiple impacts, benefits, and possible mitigation measures
Reject all evidence about the project's benefits
Assume every energy source has identical environmental effects

questions.question: An aquifer receives about 10 million liters of recharge annually while pumping removes 14 million liters. Which change most directly addresses the imbalance?
choices: Reduce withdrawals or increase feasible recharge while monitoring aquifer conditions
Measure only one well once
Assume recharge rises whenever pumping rises
Pump faster during dry periods
